name: Pidilite Industries Ltd
title: Pidilite Industries Ltd - 500331 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue +22.2% on 11.3% underlying volume growth with price hikes of 2–12%; gross margin fell 90bp to 52.5% yet EBITDA margin rose to 26.4%, flattered by low-cost inventory that management says will unwind in Q2.

summary.headline: Pidilite Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 22.2% to INR4,237 crores with 11.3% underlying volume growth; EBITDA margin 26.4%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 22.2% to INR4,237 crores, with underlying volume growth (UVG) of 11.3%, led by Consumer and Bazaar at 12.2% while B2B UVG was 7.3%. Gross margin was 52.5%, down 90 bps YoY, but total costs below gross margin rose only 14.5%, lifting EBITDA margin to 26.4% (up 80 bps QoQ) and PAT up 27.7%. Consolidated revenue rose 21.3% to INR4,541 crores with PAT up 30.3%. Management attributed part of the margin strength to pre-cost inventory, moderating schemes and proactive replacement-margin pricing, and flagged that some of this will reverse in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: A&P and sales promotion were a large part

segments.name: Consumer and Bazaar (standalone)
segments.commentary: UVG of 12.2% in Q1; management called it a step up from FY26 full-year UVG of about 11.1% and said it sees this as a normal trend.

segments.name: B2B (standalone)
segments.commentary: UVG of 7.3%, held back by exports, where B2B export UVG was -8.4% amid geopolitical disruption in key markets.

segments.name: Domestic subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11.5%; Consumer and Bazaar in domestic subsidiaries grew 17%, while B2B grew 3.5%.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 12%, with Bangladesh, Egypt and Kenya growing well above their past rates.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin corridor of 20% to 24% retained; management said no change needed now, with margins having fallen to the high teens during the steep input-cost spike.
Management said margins could moderate in Q2 as lower-cost inventory unwinds, but it could be middle to higher end of the band for the year if crude stays around mid-80s and volatility eases.
Management expects some time-weighted price benefit to flow into Q2 and Q3, partly offset by rebates on VAM-linked products.
Management expects double-digit UVG over the medium term, aiming to inch it up, with core categories growing at 1x to 2x GDP.
Export volumes expected to recover as geopolitical situation normalises, as most contracts remain in place.
capex_capacity: Nio Pro (launched about two quarters ago via the Spanish JV) expanding from 1 plant to 4 plants for wider geographic availability.
Tile adhesives: company is expanding its plant network and investing in plant automation and quality consistency.
No specific capex amount or commissioning timeline was disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: Consumer and Bazaar price increases ranged from about 2% to 12% by category and brand; most pricing went into the market by June, and some was phased through the quarter.
No demand impact from price increases seen so far; management said Bazaar projects are budgeted upfront and ongoing projects are not stopped.
Some pre-buying or upstocking by channel likely in Q1 from multiple price increases, per management.
VAM prices moved from about $800-900 to near $2,000 and then fell; Q1 VAM consumption averaged $1,370 vs $924 a year ago and about $800 in Q4. Company is passing some rebates to customers.
Competitors follow price increases and rebates closely, according to management.
Tile adhesive penetration in India is at most 25-30%; a South India cement company is entering tile adhesives. Management said it is growing fastest in the category and gaining share.
Waterproofing (Dr. Fixit): management said it is growing in the mid-teens, with momentum in retail and projects via trained applicators and systems specification.

qa_highlights.question: Will export demand bounce back after geopolitical issues resolve, and did competitors take share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most export contracts remain in place and volumes will return as the situation normalises, though some customers may have made alternate arrangements.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of a large paint company's new VAM/VAE capacity on Pidilite's cost and pricing position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Pidilite runs a brand-led, market-sourcing model, does not expect material change, and has revisited the matter with key suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the double-digit price hike too much now that VAM has fallen; are trade margins rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is giving some rebates as VAM moves, was more proactive this time, and competitors are following its prices and rebates; it said it had absorbed part of the cost hit earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Will C&B UVG of about 12% (vs 15% last quarter) sustain; any June moderation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no monthly moderation, described 12.5% C&B UVG as a step up on the 3-year trend, and said demand is holding well.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 margins benefit from cheaper inventory, and will gross margin fall back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed three Q1 benefits: replacement-margin pricing, carry-over lower-cost inventory, and moderating schemes. Some of this will reverse in Q2, but H1 is not a major concern according to the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Could margins sit at the top of the 20-24% band this year at mid-80s crude?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said middle to higher end of the band is possible if crude stays around mid-80s and volatility eases, but cautioned it is a big if.

risks_watch: Export recovery timing given geopolitical disruption (B2B exports UVG -8.4%).
Q2 margin reversal as lower-cost inventory is consumed and higher-priced inventory flows through.
VAM and crude volatility, plus rebates that could offset time-weighted price gains.
Rising competition in tile adhesives from cement and tile makers and existing players.
Competition in waterproofing from multinationals and local players.
UnoFin is early-stage; no revenue target was given beyond a review of the base around next year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and demand, saying demand is holding well and there is no monthly slowdown. More cautious on margins, calling Q1 a high point with some moderation likely in Q2, and gave evasive answers on UnoFin revenue and specific competitor moves.
key_quotes: And I can tell you very, very categorically that the demand is holding quite well.
So most of the pricing have gone in, in June. We've not seen any substantial impact.
But if you look at a normalized H1, I would not say there is any major concern on that.
And I think that's a step up on our previous year, which was 9-point something.

adds.what: Nio Pro expanding from 1 plant to 4 plants (via Spanish JV) for wider geographic availability

growth.why: Q1 standalone revenue grew 22.2% with 11.3% UVG (C&B 12.2%, B2B 7.3%), and management reiterates double-digit medium-term UVG and a 20-24% EBITDA margin corridor, but gave no quantified capacity, capex or order-book numbers behind it and flagged a Q2 margin moderation.
